Alex — great to meet you and thanks for the detailed recap. Attaching a short proposed integration plan and a high-level architecture diagram to start. See answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

1) SDK + auth:
- We support both API keys and service-account style credentials (OIDC tokens/service accounts) for Private deployments. For hosted, API keys are the default; for Private you can configure short-lived service account credentials integrated with your IdP or KMS.
- Recommendation: prototype with API keys on hosted, then switch to service-account/OIDC when you move to VPC.

2) Tool definitions (recommended pattern):
- Use a small, explicit tool schema with: name, inputs (typed), sync/async flag, timeout_ms, success_schema (JSON Schema for structured output), and error_policy (fail_fast | partial | fallback).
- Example (high-level):
  {"name": "get_account_details", "inputs": ["account_id"], "sync": true, "timeout_ms": 500, "success_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"balance":{"type":"number"}}}}
- Keep tool payloads narrow (one intent per tool) to reduce ambiguity and make reranking predictable.

3) Parallel tools + re-rankers:
- Pattern A (Parallel enrichment + merge + rerank):
  - Fire enrichment calls in parallel with reasonable timeouts (e.g., 300-600ms).
  - Aggregate partial results as they arrive, normalize to a common candidate schema, then call a reranker model (lightweight embedding-based or fine-tuned ranker) to score candidates.
  - If one enrichment call times out, proceed with available candidates; mark missing data for the assistant to surface.
- Pattern B (Staged: fast-first + background enrich):
  - Call the fastest, highest-confidence tool synchronously to surface an immediate answer. Kick off slower enrichments in background and surface an updated answer or link when ready.

4) Error handling recommendations:
- Default: use partial mode (error_policy: partial) so the assistant can still return a best-effort response.
- Implement per-tool timeouts, circuit-breaker (fail open after N errors), and a graceful fallback tool (e.g., a generic KB lookup) if enrichment consistently fails.
- Include provenance metadata (tool_name, confidence, timestamp) in structured output for downstream auditing.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed-integration-plan.pdf], [Attachment: high-level-arch.png]

Code & docs:
- SDKs: Python and Java SDK samples available here: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/overview

  tools = [\"get_account_details\", \"credit_enrich\"]
  resp = client.call_with_tools(prompt, tools=tools, parallel=True, timeout_ms=800)

Alex — quick answers and confirmation for the deep-dive invite: 

- Auth: Yes — Redwood Private accepts OIDC-issued short-lived tokens. For some IdPs we provide a lightweight exchange sidecar, but most customers integrate directly via OIDC service accounts. Dylan will walk through the exact flow in the deep dive.
- Routing: Yes — routing rules can be specified per-call via the SDK (region, model_variant, tier). We support policy-based routing (latency vs cost) and explicit pinning.
- Tool-def & provenance: Attached example tool-def includes success_schema and an additional metadata block we recommend for provenance (tool_name, call_latency_ms, confidence).
- Java snippet: We'll include a small Spring/Java example showing parallel CompletableFuture calls + handling partials and a simple fallback.
